The largest decreases in the CD4 cell count during treatment interruptions occur in patients with a lower nadir CD 4 cell count or with more advanced disease.

The largest decreases in absolute CD4 cell counts during treatment interruptions occurred in those with lower nadir counts and more advanced disease; the greatest CD4 cell losses were observed in those with higher baseline CD4 cell losses before highly active antretroviral therapy and those who had higher rates of CD8 cell increases during the treatment interruption; and treatment interruptions were associated with a significant increased risk of clinical/AIDS events in those with lower baseline nadir CD4 counts and higher baseline CD8 cell counts.
